messages:
Alex: kicking off a short thread — BigCorp POC. they want multi-region dedicated capacity (eu + us) and SSO + KMS. can we confirm pricing and any blockers?
Maria: thanks. main asks i heard: reserved capacity in eu, SSO via SAML, customer KMS for key wrapping, low-latency 99th pct spikes. also they want to try quantized models to cut cost.
Sam: quick note — quantization can change output slightly. we should run a quality eval against their prompt set before recommending 8-bit.
Jordan: +1. also streaming tool/function calls are in scope. they plan to use our streaming SDK (ws) and do structured outputs to parse transactions.
Lisa: Security asked for SOC2 cert, data residency guarantee for EU region, and an encrypted-at-rest KMS handshake doc. legal will want the key-handling diagram.
Ben: for pricing: reserved dedicated nodes in eu region — baseline quote is $Xk/mo per 8-GPU pool at 99% utilization. with cross-region failover add ~20%. if they want burst capacity it changes SLAs. i can pull an official quote — need expected qps and tokens/day.
Alex: they estimated 125 qps peak, avg 40 qps, 2b tokens/mo. can we get a sample pricing table?
Ben: noted. that token volume with dedicated will likely move to a committed tier. i'll draft numbers and share.
Maria: on integration: sample streaming init we suggest for SDKs:
```
# curl websocket upgrade sample
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-3b-quant
```
Also remind them to enable `adaptive_batching: true` in the SDK config to smooth latency/cost tradeoffs.
Sam: adaptive batching note: recommend target latency of 120ms for UI flows; for lower latency ops (backend sync) set batch window to 30ms. quantify perf on their prompt lengths.
Jordan: structured output schema they want looks like: `{"transaction_id": string, "amount": number, "merchant": {"id": string}}`. we'll need to provide a validate/schema example and show stable parsing with function-calling fallback.
Lisa: security-bot ran quick checks — we still need onprem KMS guide and confirmation that ephemeral creds are supported for streaming connections. Security-Bot: SOC2 Type II doc link: https://redwood.ai/compliance/soc2 (access restricted), KMS integration guide: internal ticket #SEC-412.
Security-Bot: note: multi-region dedicated will require VPC peering or Private deployment for EU-only processing requirement. flag to infra.
Seana: i'll take point on the POC runbook. proposed plan: 1) SE call to collect promptset + traffic profile, 2) run baseline with fp16 model, 3) run quantized eval + diff thresholds, 4) demo streaming SDK + structured output, 5) finalize reserved quote and SLA.
Alex: perfect. blockers we anticipate: legal on KMS & data residency, perf regressions from quant, and ops for multi-region network egress. who owns each?
Lisa: security/infosec owns KMS/legal; i'll loop in Legal.
Ben: pricing/finance will own the quote and committed tier. i'll drop initial numbers by EOD.
Sam: i'll spin up a small eval harness and run the quant vs fp16 on their promptset once we get it. need sample prompts and expected correctness metric.
Maria: can we schedule a 30m sync with BigCorp on Tue 10am CET? i'll send calendar invite once SE confirms.
Alex: thanks team. action items: Ben = quote, Sam = eval harness, Seana = runbook & meeting, Lisa = legal loop. ping here when done. :thumbsup:
